Linus and Luke discuss the UK fining Reddit £14.5 million for failing to properly verify user ages. They explore the tension between government-mandated data collection and user privacy, noting Reddit’s reliance on self-declared ages and the Persona verification system. They also critique the broader issue of over-collecting sensitive data on children, highlighting that enforcement often fails to protect the most at-risk users while creating massive troves of data vulnerable to misuse.
